claims.head: Who drives the play: the Lightning
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Lightning have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Rangers around the middle. The ice should tilt the Lightning’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 5 games, including the last one. Gage Goncalves takes shifts on two lines, L1 and L4. Victor Hedman is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Crozier and Černák.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 38% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 28 seconds at a time, against 69 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (8 of 12 changes).

notes.text: Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 44% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

stakes: The Lightning go in tied for second in the Atlantic with 8 points, the Rangers second in the Metropolitan with 10 points.

NYR.head: The Rangers start a half-step behind
NYR.body: Even though the Rangers have home-ice advantage, Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Rangers’ best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

TBL.head: Leaning the Lightning’s way
TBL.body: Even though the Rangers have home-ice advantage, Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Rangers can still swing it if their power play gets going.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Rangers won the first meeting this season, 5-1 in New York. The Rangers are 5-2-0. The Lightning have won four straight.
The Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Rangers do. The Bolts shoot a lot, but the Rangers don’t.
